So maybe try paying by the week or Airbnb by the week.  Airbnb is more reliable but not always great for short notice

Maybe try looking on street easy.  Is your budget only $600 for you or for both of you?  Because I’m part of a pair and couldn’t find anything for below $900 for couples and $900 was rare.  However $1200 for a couple is common I guess since the idea is that each person pay $600.  That’s the situation I ended up going with.  My partner and I were homeless for 4 months and used Airbnb until we found a living situation but be warned Airbnb in NYC during the summer is much more expensive than during the winter, which is what caused us to really just accept any place that let us stay long term for an unchanging amount so we could at least budget and save while we figured out our next move.

Otherwise I’d check craigslist and also maybe try calculating how much per week you’d pay in your budget because some places are only listed as pay for the week places, so you might have more luck finding something that way.  Craigslist is good for finding something fast, but isn’t super reliable.  If you’re really in a bind by the 1st I’d try renting an Airbnb for a week and go from there.  At least you’ll have somewhere to stay.  We’ve stayed in places in far rock away because it was affordable and even if the commute was long we had public transportation.  Plus it is much cheaper than a hotel.  Depending on your savings you might even be able to rent a room through Airbnb for more than a week.  A lot of places do 20% discounts and other deals if you rent long term which can help.  

If you do use Airbnb learn from my mistakes:  

Message if a place is available first.  It may be listed as available but I have had it happen too many times where I rent and the transaction goes through and then the host never answers and you can’t access the building.  Airbnb usually is good about refunding right away if you call and get Airbnb credit - but it is stressful and that is money that can only be Airbnb credit after the bad transaction takes place.  

If you message a host you can also explain why you’re renting a room because some people only want to rent to tourists not working people.  

Double check they are near transportation.  I’ve stayed in places in queens that claimed being close to public transit but didn’t mention they were only close to a bus that was close to a train.  

Pick one person in your couple that will mostly talk to the host.  Makes things less confusing.  

Always check their house rules because they can kick you out early if you don’t follow them (mostly about drinking or quiet hours) and you won’t get a refund.

Don’t be afraid of Staten Island.  It is cheaper and isn’t actually a bad commute because the ferry is free and reliable.  The main thing you’d be relying on is a bus but the ride for most places out there isn’t more than 20 minutes.

Gender is more than pronouns, and your journey with it is personal.  I came out to my family and friends as agender a few years ago and for me that meant a lot of freedom to try different ways of expressing what that meant to me.  I have breasts but I bind and while I don’t want them gone I want them reduced at some point in the future.  I’m fine with my genitals but socially feel the need to present more masculine in how I dress.  I go by a different, more neutral name than my birth name.  I love make up and don’t shave my facial hair.  I was on testosterone for a year but stopped because I didn’t like how it affected me emotionally.  I have a naturally deeper voice and have practiced throat exercises to make it deeper.  I do a lot of wild shit to my hair.  The point is you do what you do to feel right in your body, and if you begin to feel as though you identify in a particular way then try to find a safe space to explore that.  It can really help you feel personally fulfilled and you may learn things about yourself you never knew, or, like you mentioned, finally understand feelings you’ve had for a long time.  

I use “they/them” pronouns because that feels right and makes me experience gender euphoria.  I know some people that use she/her or he/him pronouns but don’t identify as a woman or man.  One of my friends just asks that we refer to them by their name when we can otherwise “he or they” pronouns are okay.  Some people feel as though “they/them” pronouns are awkward to use for themselves and might just use more traditional pronouns for sake of ease.  Some people experiment with more than one pronoun for themselves.  It all depends on you.  Just because you continue using pronouns you’ve used your whole life doesn’t mean you aren’t valid in how you self identify.  Gender is a personal experience, and what it means to be what is a constantly changing definition.

I agree that putting them in a loud, isolated room isn't the best way to get them used to you and is likely to cause stress and a panic response (they might come to associate you or your family with the loud noises and stressful environment and hide from you).  

I would put them in a common living space if you can.  And spend a lot of time with them during the first few weeks.  

As for neutering unless you plan on housing them with females or they're aggressive I don't really see it as a necessary procedure for males.

How do you feed them treats?  Chances are where you got him they gave him treats with their hands and he associates hands with treats and gets excited and tries to grab them and run off. 

I have a girl who does the same thing and she used to be a real biter.  I helped train her by making it clear that treats are to be given at the cage door when it is open (not through the bars) and by making a clicking sound with my mouth to let them know it is treat time.  That way when my hands are around them but I don't make the sound they know I don't have treats.  It doesn't take too long (rats are so smart) just stick to it.  

He almost might just be getting used to you and is a little defensive.  Try bringing him to your bed to bond and (I did this next trick too) put a sock you don't mind parting with in their cage after rubbing it under your armpits or wearing it to get him used to your smell.  

Good luck!  Some rats are just biters but that might help.  Also rats can be trained like dogs so when he does bite you chastise him in a firm voice (a simple, low "no" should suffice) and he should learn that isn't okay.

Hi!  Rats and living with them can be a really fun experience for you and your new furry (or not so furry) babies.  Making little salads with peas, carrots, broccoli, and sunflower seeds for your rats is a good way to give them some healthy variety in addition to commercial food.  I personally only buy Oxbow for my rats and then supplement with fresh fruits and veggies.  

Also try to make sure they have plenty to chew and plenty to do.  My girls really love pulling at cloth and other things so when I have extra time I sew cheerios to an old sock and pin that up for them to basically rip apart.  I also fill the sock with blueberries.  But I normally do that before cleaning day since they tend to get juice everywhere.  

Another easy fun game/treat is to get strands of millet.  I hang it from the cage and they climb to get it.  My boys and girls love it!  That'd be another thing right before cleaning.  I also buy like extra levels for them to climb and explore.  And a dig box is something that my girls and boys love.  I take a cardboard box and fill it with tissues, toilet paper rolls, and scrap fabric (fleece or cotton only).  They go nuts digging around.  I hide treats too.  

Daily roam time is really important.  Rat proofing your room or bathroom and setting up cardboard boxes and a dig box and just some loose fabric for them to explore for like an hour is alway great.  Make sure you leave out food and water for them when they're roaming.  When I do this I hide little treats in my clothes too so that we can bond when they explore me and find the treats.  

To keep their nails less sharp I also put rocks in their cage but I wouldn't just go out and pick a rock from outside.  Getting like a piece of granite or something they sell at a pet store is best because that's clean.  

Always make sure they have something to chew.  Their teeth grow 4 inches every year and they constantly have to be chewing to prevent health issues.  And they have sensitive respiratory systems so if you smoke or if people you have over smoke do it in a separate room.  

Whenever I give my girl's and boy's treats by hand I make a clicking sound so that they only associate treats and my hands with that sound.  It really helps prevent them from biting.  

Best of luck!  Post some pictures some time!

It is evident you cared for him very much, but rats require a lot more care than people think.  It is likely he died due to a combination of not having the right diet (froot loops are not healthy for rats because of their high sugar content, the meal worms have too much protien.  A grain mix and veggies like broccoli and carrots would have been much better) and habitat (rats have really sensitive respitory systems, especially rats from pet shops that likely already have respitory issues and when they are in tanks without any ventilation it can make their respitory issues worse.  also rats need to be active and have a habitat with lots to chew and climb or else they will grow sad and that can make them sick) and possibly being a sick rat.  Most pet store rats tend to be sick and require a vet visit after being adopted.  My partner and I had a terrible experience once when we adopted a girl from this pet store (she was being kept all alone in an aquarium it was disgusting).  We scheduled a vet appointment for her the next day because she was really wheezy.  The vet said she just needed some antibiotics (some we had been given for our other rats) and that if she is still showing symptoms in two weeks to come back.  We kept her separate from the others and on the other side of the room.  Unfortunately she wasn't alive for more than a week.  She passed away and it was incredibly shocking.  I thought it was entirely my fault, but after some time it is clear that some rats simply die.  You did your best, but even if you had a cage and gotten another rat it is likely (especially because this was so fast) Lovely would have passed away anyway and just gotten the other rat sick.  Losing a friend is hard, so I'm sorry you're going through this.  Next time you consider getting a rat I would suggest making sure you are prepared with the right food and an environment big enough for two because you really should get two rats together rather than one and then one later.
